sweep_summary: Bunun (bunu1267) is in the catalog as MORPHOLOGICAL on De Busser 2009 (Takivatan: penultimate stress counted on the root, only focus -un/-an shift it). The sweep list had one item, Huang 2008 (Linguistics 46.1, Isbukun + Takituduh dialects): relevant to word stress, but paywalled at De Gruyter with no open copy anywhere checked (Unpaywall, Semantic Scholar, CORE, OpenAlex, Academia Sinica Scholars Hub, Wayback, researchgate/thefreelibrary bot pages); its abstract (OpenAlex) says Isbukun has unmarked penultimate stress that shifts to final position when a heavy syllable would otherwise be in weak position, and Takituduh keeps disyllabic feet, i.e. the same base-penult rule plus quantity sensitivity, so it refines the record (weight fields) rather than the verdict; priority high to acquire. Two extra first-hand sources were read: (1) Ouyang 2012 'Stress and Suffixation in Isbukun Bunun' (Coyote Papers 20, pp. 100-108), recovered from the Wayback Machine since repository.arizona.edu returns 403; it states for Isbukun a single right-edge moraic trochee (final heavy = long vowel/diphthong stressed, else penultimate; codas weightless; no secondary stress) with inflectional suffixes and clitics never stressed and derivational suffixes (-un/-an etc.) shifting stress rightward. This is the best new statement: it confirms the morphological verdict for a second dialect and refines the catalog's 'weight_class: not-applicable' as Takivatan-only, but does not supersede the deciding thesis. (2) De Busser's 2011 NTHU handout (already on file; URL confirmed at rdbusser.com/), sec. 3.5, restates the thesis rule verbatim in substance and confirms the catalog. A Brill Handbook of Formosan Languages 'Bunun' chapter (De Busser & Li, doi:10.1163/2772-5766_hflo_com_305050) exists but is paywalled and unread (priority medium). All fetches and metadata records are and listed in there. searching was done through OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, Unpaywall, CORE, Wayback and direct fetches.

new_statements.quote: In Isbukun Bunun, coda consonants do not contribute to syllable weight. Syllables with a long vowel (CV:C) or diphthong (CVVC) are heavy, and syllables with a short vowel (CVC) are light. A single quantity-sensitive trochee is formed at the right edge of a word (Huang 2008), as shown in (1). (1) a. Stress falls on the final syllable if it is heavy. L(ˈH)# si.la.(ˈla:) 'provoke; challenge' H(ˈH)# ma.aun.(ˈvai) 'win in arm wrestling' b. If the final syllable is light, stress falls on the penultimate syllable. (ˈLL)# pi.(ˈnas.kal) 'make happy' (ˈH)L# i.(ˈais).ku 'near to'

new_statements.reading: Isbukun Bunun (a different dialect from the catalog's Takivatan): one right-edge moraic trochee; final syllable stressed if heavy (long vowel or diphthong; codas weightless), otherwise penultimate; no secondary stress. Morphological conditioning as in Takivatan: derivational suffixes (incl. focus -un/-an) are inside the stress domain and pull stress rightward, inflectional suffixes (-in, -aŋ), determiners and pronominal clitics are never stressed and leave base stress in place (sec. 2.4, 2.6: 'inflectional suffixes and clitics are never stressed'). So the catalog's MORPHOLOGICAL verdict holds for Isbukun too, but the record's weight fields ('weight_class: not-applicable', vowel length non-phonemic) are Takivatan-specific: Isbukun is quantity-sensitive (long vowel / diphthong = heavy) with the same base-penult default. This is the first-hand Isbukun statement the catalog flagged as unreached.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both deciding passages (2.5.2 pp. 149-150 and 3.2.2.B p. 168) are verbatim in the held extracted text of De Busser 2009 at the stated line numbers; page locators match the footers. (2) The deciding source is the 711-pp fieldwork PhD grammar of Takivatan Bunun, Glottolog's top-ranked grammar for bunu1267 and the only full English description; nothing better exists for this variety, and the author's 2011 handout (fetched sources now, p. 9) restates the identical rule (root-penultimate stress; -in does not shift; -un/-an shift). (3) The only gap is dialect coverage: the record is keyed to the language-level code while the stress literature for Isbukun/Takituduh (Huang 2008, Ouyang 2012) is unread -- abstracts indicate penultimate default with suffix extrametricality (consistent in spirit) plus weight/onset-conditioned final stress in Isbukun; both remain unfetched (403 / paywall). sources.note: First-hand description of the Isbukun dialect (speakers from Hualien, Kaohsiung, Nantou, Taitung; Kaohsiung variant used where they disagree). Primary stress only, no secondary stress. A single moraic trochee at the right edge: final heavy syllable (long vowel or diphthong; codas do not count) is stressed, otherwise penultimate. Long vowels occur only in stressed stem-final syllables and shorten when made non-final. Morphology: derivational suffixes (focus -un/-an, imperative -a/-av/-aŋ, diminutive -að) are footed and stress shifts rightward onto the new penult/final heavy (ma.(ˈsa.bah) 'slee…

sources.citation: De Busser, Rik. 2011. Introduction to the Bunun language. Handout, 'Languages of Taiwan', 14 May 2011 (23 pp). https://www.rdbusser.com/talks/
sources.quote: 'Most words in Bunun have penultimate stress on the word root. This means that stress falls on the second-to-last syllable of the form that remains when you take away all the affixes. qaisiŋ [ˈqai.sɪŋ], baluku [ba.ˈlu.ku], haðun-in [ˈha.ðu.nin] (stress is not changed by the suffix -in). Some affixes do change the stress, such as the undergoer focus suffix -un and the locative focus suffix -an. liskin [ˈlɪʃ.kɪn] (penultimate) but: in-liskin-an [ɪn.lɪʃ.ˈkiː.nan] (last root syllable)'
sources.note: Same author and same rule as the catalog's deciding source (De Busser 2009 thesis): penultimate stress counted on the root with affixes stripped; -in and other affixes invisible; -un/-an shift stress rightward. Stated for 'Bunun' in a handout that covers Takivatan and Isbukun, but the examples are the Takivatan ones from the thesis; no weight statement.
